summary:
Aswanna.AI is a climate-smart agricultural decision-support platform developed to help Sri Lankan farmers make informed, data-driven crop-planning decisions using NASA Earth-observation data and local agricultural information.

The platform integrates NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, SRTM and MODIS GIBS datasets with Sri Lankan soil, crop, yield and market statistics. Using machine learning and multi-criteria decision analysis, it evaluates crop suitability, water availability, soil health, agricultural risks and potential income to generate location-specific crop recommendations. It also incorporates a national market safeguard to prevent widespread crop shifts from causing excessive price fluctuations. Farmers can access recommendations through a multilingual web interface, while agricultural officers and policymakers can use a national dashboard to assess production trends and resource requirements.

Aswanna.AI addresses the growing challenges of climate variability, agricultural uncertainty and food security. By transforming satellite observations into practical agricultural insights, it aims to support sustainable farming, improve resource efficiency and strengthen national agricultural planning.
details:
The platform integrates NASA Earth-observation datasets, including NASA POWER, GPM IMERG, SRTM and MODIS GIBS, with local agricultural, soil, historical yield and market data. Using machine learning (LightGBM) and multi-criteria decision analysis (TOPSIS), it evaluates crop suitability, rainfall patterns, water availability, soil health, agricultural risks and potential income. Farmers can select their location and priorities to receive ranked crop recommendations for the Maha and Yala seasons, together with estimated income ranges, explanations and risk warnings.

A key innovation is its national market safeguard, which considers the collective impact of farmers following similar recommendations. This helps prevent excessive crop-price fluctuations while supporting individual farm profitability. The platform also includes a national dashboard and harvest outlook to help agricultural officers and policymakers understand potential production, resource requirements and crop surpluses or shortages. Multilingual access, offline data availability and alternative access through Telegram and agricultural officers are incorporated to improve accessibility.

The project was developed using Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, React, HTML and CSS within a server-based environment, with Firebase supporting backend services. Visual Studio Code was used as the primary development environment and GitHub for version control and team collaboration. AI-assisted tools were incorporated throughout development: Claude Opus 5.5 helped refine the proposed system architecture and optimize team-developed code, while GitHub Copilot supported code optimization. Google Gemini was used for prototype UI design, and Gemini Pro provided secondary reviews to improve the structure and quality of project content. Gamma AI assisted in generating presentation materials, which were subsequently refined using Microsoft PowerPoint. These tools complemented the team's own design, implementation and decision-making.

The creative aspect of Aswanna.AI lies in combining satellite-based environmental intelligence, local agricultural knowledge, machine learning and economic analysis into one decision-support system. Rather than simply recommending crops based on environmental conditions, it considers long-term soil health, water conservation, farmer income and national market stability together.

The intended impact is to strengthen climate resilience, promote sustainable agricultural practices, improve farmers' livelihoods and support better-informed planning.
